architecture.mechanism: Multilingual natural-language interface integrated with a standardized control stack to allow interactive exploration of parameter trade-offs and enforce bounded operational envelopes via automated control.
architecture.intervention: Add a watchdog layer to the engine start-stop and remote-start control stack that uses a rule-based control policy (analogous to an EPICS/Bluesky-style structured control interface) to monitor ignition duration, automatically issue an engine shutdown command when a configurable timeout (e.g., one hour) is reached, and only release control for normal user-initiated start-stop or remote-start commands when safe conditions are confirmed.
architecture.expected_effect: Unattended engine operation is capped at the bounded timeout, preventing prolonged idling, while preserving normal user-driven start-stop and remote-start functionality, thereby mitigating fire, carbon-monoxide, and theft hazards.
architecture.falsification_test: In a vehicle or hardware-in-the-loop simulation, trigger an unattended remote-start idle and verify that (a) the engine shuts off within the configured timeout without user input, (b) a subsequent user-initiated remote-start command still starts the engine normally, and (c) normal key-on start-stop cycles (e.g., at traffic lights) are unaffected and do not trigger premature shutdown.
